server.name: Simply.com
server.description: Simply.com MCP Server - Public tools for domain checks and help articles

live.instructions:
Simply.com public MCP Server.

Available tools:
- check-domain-availability: verify if a domain is available for registration or transfer. Each response includes a purchase_link and a tld_info_link.
- create-order-link: build a prefilled order link for one or more domains (new registrations, or transfers when an auth code is supplied). Returns a checkout URL the user visits to complete and pay for the order; works whether or not they are signed in.
- list-supported-tlds: list all TLDs available for registration at Simply.com.
- search-docs: search the Simply.com help articles (web hosting, domains, DNS, email, databases, SSL and the control panel) and get their full Markdown content. Use it to answer how-to and troubleshooting questions with Simply.com's own documentation.

Once a user has signed up and has a Simply.com account, they can connect to the authenticated MCP at https://mcp.simply.com/v2 (OAuth 2.1) to manage their products: list products, manage DNS records, registrar settings (nameservers, DNSSEC), mail accounts and forwards, subdomains, MySQL databases, website and MySQL slow logs, deploy details, support tickets, and more. Setup instructions for AI agents are at https://www.simply.com/agent-setup/prompt.md.

For operations not covered by these MCP servers, use the Simply.com REST API at https://api.simply.com (documentation at https://www.simply.com/docs/api/).

tools.name: search-docs

query.description: What to search for, as keywords or a natural-language question, e.g. "IMAP settings for Outlook"

limit.description: Maximum number of articles to return

tools.description: Search the Simply.com support FAQ (help articles about web hosting, domains, DNS, email, databases, SSL and the control panel). Articles are in English and the query may be in any language. Returns the best matching articles with their full Markdown content and a link to each article. Each article has a category, e.g. "PHP" (Linux web hosting) or "ASP & ASP.NET" (Windows web hosting), "MySQL" or "Microsoft SQL Server": only rely on articles whose category matches the user's product. Use it to answer how-to and troubleshooting questions with Simply.com's own documentation, e.g. mail client settings, PHP versions or how to change nameservers.

tools.name: check-domain-availability

domain.description: The full domain name to check, e.g. "example.com" or "example.dk"

type.description: Which checks to run. "register" (the default) reports whether the domain can be registered. "transfer" reports whether it can be transferred, and should only be used for a domain already known to be registered.

tools.description: Check if a domain name is available for registration at Simply.com. When the domain can be registered and the user wants to order it, use the create-order-link tool to generate a checkout link.

tools.name: list-supported-tlds
tools.description: Lists every top-level domain (TLD) Simply.com can register, each with a link to its info page, plus a total count. Use it to answer which extensions are on offer, or to confirm a TLD is supported before checking a specific name. It returns no prices, and it does not say whether an individual domain is free: use check-domain-availability for that.

tools.name: create-order-link

domains.description: The domains to add to the order.

domain.description: The full domain name to order, e.g. "example.com" or "example.dk".

action.description: Whether to register a new domain or transfer an already-registered domain into Simply.com. Defaults to "register".

auth_code.description: Optional transfer authorization / EPP code for a transfer. Not required for all TLDs; omit it if the user does not have one.

tools.description: Create a prefilled Simply.com order link for one or more domains. Returns a checkout URL the user visits to complete and pay for the order. Each domain is a new registration by default, or an inbound transfer when action is "transfer". The link works whether or not the user is signed in: existing customers sign in at checkout, new customers create an account. Check availability with check-domain-availability first.
